title: Vanishing for a finite filtered augmented simplex first page
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and use its ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a nonempty finite linearly ordered set of cardinality $m$. Let $D\in D(\mathcal A)$ have a finite decreasing filtration by distinguished triangles: objects $F^aD$, maps $F^{a+1}D\to F^aD$, identifications $F^{-1}D=D$, $F^mD=0$, and distinguished triangles $F^{a+1}D\to F^aD\to G^a\to F^{a+1}D[1]$ for $-1\le a<m$. The first page of its cohomological exact-couple spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] is $E_1^{a,b}=\mathcal H^{a+b}(G^a)$ with differential of bidegree $(1,0)$. Suppose for every integer $b$ an object $M_b\in\mathcal A$ and isomorphisms identify this row, including its differential, with the augmented alternating subset complex
$$M_b\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=1}M_b\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=2}M_b\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=m}M_b,$$
where $J$ ranges over subsets of $I$, the augmentation object has horizontal degree $-1$, its map is diagonal, and the component of the differential at $a_0<\cdots<a_{n+1}$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j c(a_0,\ldots,\widehat{a_j},\ldots,a_{n+1})$. Terms outside $-1\le a<m$ are zero.
Then $D$ is a zero object of $D(\mathcal A)$. No boundedness in the cohomology degree $b$ and no strict chain-level identification of the graded objects are required. In particular, if $D$ is a cone of a morphism $u$, then $u$ is an isomorphism. The assertion is invariant under maps of such filtered data. It concerns a finite filtration; it asserts no convergence for infinite filtrations or infinite totalizations.

proof.text: Fix $b$ and write $C^a$ for its displayed augmented subset row. Choose the least vertex $v\in I$. Define $h^a:C^a\to C^{a-1}$ by finite biproduct matrices: for $a\geq0$, the component indexed by a subset $J$ of size $a$ is $c_{\{v\}\cup J}$ if $v\notin J$, and zero if $v\in J$; $v$ is first in the ordered union. Thus $h^0$ is projection to the vertex $v$. Put $h^{-1}=0$ and extend the maps by zero beyond the row. The notation $c_J$ denotes a biproduct projection, so the formulas define morphisms in $\mathcal A$, without assuming elements of its objects.

source.place: Agent-written least-vertex contraction of the augmented subset row; the item source explicitly distinguishes this calculation from Tag 012W.

proof.text: Check $dh+hd=1$ componentwise. At a subset $J=\{a_0<\cdots<a_a\}$ not containing $v$, the two components are $\sum_j(-1)^j c_{\{v\}\cup(J\setminus\{a_j\})}$ and $c_J+\sum_j(-1)^{j+1}c_{\{v\}\cup(J\setminus\{a_j\})}$, which add to $c_J$. If $v\in J$, only the term deleting $v$ survives in $dh$, with coefficient $+1$, while $hd$ is zero. In augmentation degree $-1$, $h^0d^{-1}=1$ since the augmentation is diagonal. These identities include the top degree (a maximal subset contains $v$). Restricting $1=dh+hd$ to $\ker d$ shows that its inclusion factors through $d$; hence $\ker d=\operatorname{im}d$. Every row is exact. The assumed differential-preserving identifications and the page-homology rule of [def-sp-spectral-sequence] give $E_2^{a,b}=0$; the same rule gives zero on every later page.

source.place: Agent-written component calculation; spectral-sequence page-homology rule (Stacks 011M).

proof.text: Extend the tower constantly by $D$ for $a\leq-1$ and by zero for $a\geq m$. Use its given cohomological exact couple in the convention of [def-sp-exact-couple]: $X.D^{P,Q}=H^{P+Q}(F^{-Q}D)$ and $X.E^{P,Q}=H^{P+Q}(G^{-Q})=E_1^{-Q,P+2Q}$. Filtration inclusion has bidegree $(-1,1)$, the triangle boundary has $(2,-1)$, and the quotient map has $(0,0)$, as required. Thus the initial differential of $X$ is exactly the displayed first-page differential $d_1$; the convention calls its initial page $E_2$, so its next page is zero by step 2. For each $n$, the diagonal alpha-colimit is $A_n=H^n(D)$: $X.D^{P,n-P}=H^n(F^{P-n}D)$, the maps are identities on $H^n(D)$ for $P\leq n-1$, and the terms are zero for $P\geq n+m$. A compatible cocone is uniquely determined by its map from any constant-tail term. Apply [lem-sp-finite-cocone-exact-couple] with bounds $a_n=n-1$, $b_n=n+m$. It supplies the limiting page and identifies it with the successive quotients of the image filtration $G^P A_n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^{P-n}D)\to H^n(D))$ of [def-sp-convergence].

source.place: Tag 012W, lemma-biregular-ss-converges, finite-tail argument in the existing generic exact-couple node; explicit reindexing for a finite triangle tower.

proof.text: The limiting page in step 3 is zero because its pages after the first are zero. Therefore all $G^P A_n/G^{P+1}A_n$ vanish. Here $G^{n+m}A_n=0$ and $G^{n-1}A_n=A_n$. Descending induction over the finite interval gives $G^P A_n=0$ throughout it: a zero quotient says $G^{P+1}A_n=G^P A_n$. In particular $H^n(D)=A_n=0$ for every integer $n$. To see that this makes $D$ zero, represent it by a complex $K$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The map $K\to0$ induces isomorphisms on every cohomology object, so is a quasi-isomorphism by that definition and becomes invertible in the localization. Thus $D\cong0$. Only finitely many filtration indices were used for each $n$; there is no cohomological boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 012W, finite image-filtration argument; derived-category localization at quasi-isomorphisms (Stacks 05RU).

proof.text: If $D$ is a cone of $u$, its distinguished triangle and [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] give that $u$ is invertible. The construction of $h$ is needed only to prove zero cohomology; no chosen contraction enters the conclusion. For a map of the filtered data, the source and target objects are zero by the argument above, so its underlying morphism is the unique map between zero objects and is invertible. Every induced square between the zero cohomology objects commutes. In the cone application, any commuting square of the maps $u,u'$ also commutes after inversion: from $t u=u's$ obtain $s u^{-1}=(u')^{-1}t$ by composition. This proves the stated invariance without a functorial choice of vertex. Nothing in the proof forms an infinite filtration or totalization.
